memory_candidates.content: Before seeding an exclusion list for a new lint check from a plan's 'scope hypothesis', re-verify it LIVE against the real corpus rather than trusting the plan's line-number-derived count. On task 257's Check E, the plan hypothesized 13 exclusion entries; live verification found only 5 -- 8 files the plan assumed needed exclusion actually already passed the check on their own merit (they carried a legitimate 'failed'/'partial' branch alongside their non-canonical success vocabulary). Excluding a file that already passes silently hides it from future regression detection -- worse than doing nothing.

When a source-store shell script starts unconditionally sourcing a new shared library at top level (exit 2 if not found), every existing scratch-repo fixture test for that script must also gain a copy of the library in its scratch tree -- otherwise the test's own fixture setup breaks with an environment error before the check under test ever runs. Check for ALL scratch trees a test suite builds (a fragment-missing negative-path fixture is easy to miss since it looks unrelated to the new library).
